_comment: Home Repair — a TRADE module under Construction & Building Trades, not a core one. It is built JOB BY JOB, each done end to end rather than as a survey of maintenance, because the whole difficulty of a repair in a finished building is the work you must NOT damage, and that only shows up when one job is followed all the way through. Built by ../lesson-kit/build.py.
_extraScripts: kit.js carries every step kind this module uses (lecture, label, safety, order, browse, questions, words). tiling.js and taps.js are this module's own pictures, one file per job, and neither adds a renderer. A home-repair page loads no carpentry file and no digital one.
hubIntro: Repairs in a finished building, done without making the damage worse. Wall tiling: one broken tile out of a grouted wall and a new one back so nobody can tell which it was. And taps: reading which of the two leaks you have before you touch a spanner, and knowing when the washer is innocent.
leadsNote: No Kenyan unit codes are claimed. The only national framework in this repo is the Carpentry & Joinery Level 4 one, and it says nothing about tiling or about plumbing — so every criterion here carries an empty leadsTo until a real building-maintenance framework is in hand. A claimed code that does not exist is worse than an honest blank.
endNote: You can plan a tile replacement and a tap repair, take the old work out without damaging what stays, and read a fault before you reach for a part. What none of this gives you is the hand for it: the weight of the blow, the feel of a tile that is still holding, how far a gland nut goes past hand tight, and whether the finished work reads as a repair from a metre away. That is signed off on real work, by an assessor, and nowhere else.
